top.title: Sevilla claim late derby draw against high-flying Betis
top.description: Defender Kike Salas scored a late equaliser against Real Betis to earn Sevilla a derby draw (JORGE GUERRERO) Kike Salas struck late to save Sevilla a point in a 1-1 derby draw against Real Betis on Saturday. Manuel Pellegrini's Betis, fourth, had taken the lead through Antony's deflected effort early in the second half. However, hosts Sevilla, sixth, equalised in the 91st minute with Salas's low drive, which Betis goalkeeper Alvaro Valles somehow let squeeze past him. Betis trail leaders Barcelona by six points before the Catalan giants host Villarreal on Sunday. Later Saturday, Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid, second, host Celta Vigo, aiming to pull level with Barca at the top of the table. Elsewhere, Valencia earned a 1-0 win at Rayo Vallecano to provisionally move out of the relegation zone. Alaves defeated Deportivo La Coruna 3-1 to climb up to eighth. rbs/nf

top.title: Chelsea’s deep and ongoing issues revealed by Leeds drubbing
top.description: By the end, amid what Xabi Alonso described as a “fragile moment”, even his own cultured touch had deserted him. As his Chelsea team tried to offer something in the final minutes of an utterly nothing performance against a brilliant Leeds United , the ball was easily cleared for a throw. Alonso, famed for his technique as a player, miscontrolled it towards his underwhelming bench. He’s now seeing his reputation as a coach plummet, as Chelsea fall to eighth. This 4-1 evisceration was not just Leeds’ first win at the home of their old Seventies rivals since 1999 – to add to how Tottenham Hotspur also won here a few weeks ago – but a second defeat in a row, and a fifth in 11 this season. And yet the very nature of it was still worse than any numbers can tell. Outside an early Emmanuel Emegha goal on his first start, there was nothing to speak positively about, and just nothing about Chelsea. Leeds found it easy to get at them, and they were soon rampaging through them. They could have been 3-1 up by half-time, after Noah Okafor’s well-taken equaliser, but it never looked like it would take long to get there in the second half. And, sure, Chelsea might well dispute the absurd-looking handball decision that eventually gave Dominic Calvert-Lewin his goal to make it 2-1, but they couldn’t dispute that it was coming. Leeds were rampant, Okafor soon lashing in his second from yet another poorly-defended set-piece. There, Austin MacPhee’s influence becomes just one more aspect to question about the first team. The manner of Brenden Aaronson’s goal, as he was allowed to just surge through the team, summed the afternoon up. Chelsea didn’t look a team. Leeds, by contrast, knew exactly what they were about in every moment of the game. They had an identity. Chelsea are instead looking to individuals. Emmanuel Emegha scored Chelsea’s goal (Reuters) They lost all cohesion once Moises Caicedo again went off injured, having already lacked any bite without Joao Pedro . The striker was nevertheless involved in what might actually have been one of the match’s most telling moments. As Cole Palmer went off, Chelsea coach Willie Isa seemed to gesture the forward towards the fans. There were admittedly very few left, and many of those had loudly booed on the final whistle. Palmer didn’t go over, and then seemed to have a few words with Joao Pedro, too. They didn’t look all that amicable. “We were disappointed,” Alonso said afterwards. Either way, there is probably a bigger point there, that emphasises how all this is bigger than the manager. Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s penalty sent Leeds ahead (Reuters) Yes, a coach as accomplished as Alonso should be doing better than this. There has been constant talk that some of the players haven’t found him as tactically sophisticated as they expected, something which has arguably manifested in how they seem to have got worse the more time he’s had with them – in the same way they got worse the longer this game went on. top.title: Arsenal held by Newcastle rally and lose Raya to injury
top.description: Malick Thiaw put Newcastle in front against Arsenal (ANDY BUCHANAN) Arsenal missed the chance to open up an eight-point lead at the top of the Premier League after a stirring second-half fightback from Newcastle held the defending champions to a 2-2 draw on Saturday. The Gunners led through Eberechi Eze's strike after a dominant first 45 minutes. But Mikel Arteta's men were suddenly headed for defeat when goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw provided a much-needed boost for under-fire Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle. Noni Madueke salvaged a point for Arsenal and stretched their lead at the top over surprise package Brighton to six points. However, the loss of influential goalkeeper David Raya to injury could provide a twist in the title race that many believed Arsenal would cruise. Newcastle remain in the bottom half of the table with just one win in six games in all competitions. Yet, Jaissle can point to his side's second half performance as a potential turning point after a difficult start to his reign at St. James' Park. Arsenal move back six points clear of third-placed Manchester City, but missed the chance to put their foot down in the defence of their title. Madueke continued his impressive form in the injury absence of Bukayo Saka and hit the post early on. Former Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes was roundly booed on his first return to Tyneside since making a £75 million ($98 million) move to the Emirates Stadium In August. The Brazilian nearly silenced his former faithful when he prodded just wide from a Madueke cross as Arsenal pressed for the opener. It duly arrived 10 minutes before the break when Kai Havertz pounced on a poor touch by Lewis Hall and brilliantly played in Eze to blast high past Lukas Hornicek. Jaissle got the response he needed from his half-time team talk as Newcastle came out a completely different proposition after the break. Arsenal also played a part in letting the home side back into the game and lifting the 50,000 crowd in doing so. Martin Odegaard shanked his attempt at a long ball forward to allow William Osula to play in Barnes to level. Suddenly an Arsenal side that had kept seven clean sheets in their opening 10 league games was on the rocks. Thiaw bundled home a second for Newcastle just 13 minutes later after Dan Burn was left completely unmarked from a corner and his header was only parried by Raya. That proved to be one of Raya's final interventions as the Spaniard had to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga. Raya would be a massive miss if the Spaniard is sidelined for a significant spell. But Arsenal regained their composure in time to salvage a point that keeps them well in the driving seat to retain the title. Odegaard made amends for his earlier error by freeing Madueke down the right and he cut inside before his tame deflected shot found a way past Hornicek. kca/nf

top.title: Cardinals make bad Carson Beck news official for Week 11 vs. Chiefs
top.description: Cardinals make bad Carson Beck news official for Week 11 vs. Chiefs originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Arizona Cardinals have shuffled through multiple quarterbacks this season, starting with Jacoby Brissett for a few weeks. Gardner Minshew then got a chance, but he recently got hurt. Carson Beck stepped in, making his NFL debut and first start in Week 10. While he and the Cardinals struggled in a loss to the Los Angeles Rams , it was still nice to see Beck make his first appearance in the NFL. But the following practice week didn't go well, as back spasms sidelined him. Unfortunately, as Cardinals reporter Darren Urban shared , the team made it official: Beck is out and won't face the Kansas City Chiefs . Cardinals officially rule out Carson Beck "The AZCardinals officially downgrade QB Carson Beck to OUT for Sunday's game because of back spasms," Urban reports. "Josh Johnson gets the start in K.C." While this Cardinals team isn't contending for anything this season, one of the more important things to take away from this year is how their young players perform. It might have a low chance of happening, but if Beck impresses this season, they might have an interesting question to ask themselves at the quarterback position this upcoming offseason. But with Beck now set to miss Week 11 due to back spasms, that evaluation is on hold. Josh Johnson, the ultimate journeyman quarterback, will get the start for Arizona against the Chiefs this weekend. Beck isn't the only one this Cardinals' offense will be missing. Brissett and Marvin Harrison Jr. were traded; Minshew, James Connor, Jeremiyah Love, Kendrick Bourne, Michael Wilson, and Jalen Brooks are all out due to injury. So, while seeing Beck play is important, it would not be a surprise if he struggled with such a lackluster supporting cast, especially going up against a tough Chiefs defense, like the tough unit he faced in his NFL debut. After Beck completed 11 of 18 passes for 108 yards and no touchdowns with two picks against the Rams in Week 10, he's now going to miss his next chance to start with a back problem. The Cardinals have officially ruled out Beck for Week 11, turning to Johnson as their fourth staring quarterback they've turned to this season. top.description: AUSTIN, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 21: Head coach Steve Sarkisian of the Texas Longhorns arrives prior to the game against the Arkansas Razorbacks at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s Senior Day on the Forty Acres as quarterback Arch Manning plans to participate in what could be his final regular-season home game at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium as the No. 5 Texas Longhorns host the Arkansas Razorbacks. An SEC championship game and College Football Playoff berth are on the line for Steve Sarkisian’s team, which lost its margin for error with back-to-back losses to unranked opponents in October before surviving a home test against then-No. 7 Ole Miss and road challenges at then-No. 18 Missouri and then-No. 21 LSU. Hammack's kill gave the Lions a 27-26 advantage before a Wylie attack error ended the set. Lake Creek closed out the match with its most decisive set, punctuating the sweep with a kill from Mokry. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) Getty Images The Los Angeles Lakers sit on top of the Western Conference at 14-3, with the third-best offense in the NBA — behind an MVP-level start to the season from Luka Doncic — and a solid defense. Walker Kessler has been exactly what the Lakers hoped for as a big in the paint, and their moves for role players that better fit around Doncic — Matisse Thybulle, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Quentin Grimes, Quentin Grimes — have largely worked out. Lakers general manager Rob Pelinka has seen it, too, and thinks this team has a deep playoff run in them. Which is why he said in an interview on the Lakers pregame show that the team would be "active" at the trade deadline (hat tip Real GM ). "We'll be active at the trade deadline to shore up things that we see. We think this team has a real chance to make a run, so we want to give the group as much talent as we can. Don't want to get too far over our skis with a hot start, because you don't want to get big-headed, but clearly the way it's gone so far, it's been great, and we hope it continues." Active is a broad term. The Lakers will be active talking to teams, whether they make a deal will depend on the players available, and the price. The Lakers' most critical need is to improve at backup center behind Kessler. Kevon Looney has largely fallen out of the rotation, leaving the Lakers playing small ball with Sandro Mamukelashvili or Jarred Vanderbilt at the five, or leaning into two-way big Carson Cooper. There may be better options available. The Lakers don't have draft picks of note to trade, but they have players, and while they are hard-capped at the first apron, they are a little more than $8 million below that line and have room to work.

(Dave Zajac/Hearst Connecticut Media) We've reached the end of the line for the 2026 CIAC football regular season. Now the fun really begins. Thanksgiving football is on deck and, for 48 teams, the playoffs beyond. With at least a third of the tournament spots still open according to GametimeCT's unofficial calculations , there's plenty of drama in the final week. After a somewhat lackluster first half of the season, the second half paid off with plenty of electric games, led by Ludlowe's 34-31 win over New Canaan on Oct. 30, a game which had a wild momentum swing and jumbled the GametimeCT Top 10 Poll . The season has featured some great quarterback play, highlighted by seven senior veterans , at least six of whom will soon be in the playoff spotlight. And the list goes deeper than just those seven. For the holiday week ahead, there are 56 games involving 111 CIAC teams, with Stonington's long-running series with Westerly (R.I.) accounting for that odd number. Thanksgiving week holds plenty of drama outside of the playoff picture, with trophies, rivalry wins and bragging rights part of the scene. And the names are definitely cool. There's the Beehive Bowl between East Haven and Branford (Yellowjackets and Hornets, get it?), the Apple Valley Classic between Southington and Cheshire ; the Air and Speed Bowl between the Stafford and Windsor co-ops ; the 75th Green Bowl between Notre Dame-West Haven and Hamden ; and the Olde Canal Cup between Farmington and Plainville . Map fans will have a blast. There's the 7-Mile Bowl between Platt Tech and O'Brien Tech ; the Route 17 Bowl between the Coginchaug co-op and North Branford ; the Battle of Route 83 between Rockville and Ellington ; and even the Clash Along County Lines between the Valley Panthers and Griswold/Wheeler . There's a battle for a Boot ( Oxford-Derby ), Helmet ( Torrington-Watertown ), Bell ( Bristol Central-Bristol Eastern ), and Sword ( Ledyard-Fitch ), as well as a Battle of the Bay ( Waterford-East Lyme ). Intense rivalries are also in play, including the Stoddard Bowl between Maloney and Platt , both of whom call Falcon Field in Meriden home; the annual showdown between Ansonia and Naugatuck ; and the Turkey Bowl between New Canaan and Darien . Some of the longest-running series include Wilbur Cross , now co-oping with Career , against Hillhouse ; and the aforementioned Westerly (R.I) against Stonington . But for longevity, nothing holds a candle to New London vs. Norwich Free Academy , a series which started way back in 1875 and is the country's oldest rivalry. Enjoy the football and turkey. nigeria.title: 2027 Election: INEC failed on voters’ register – ADC
nigeria.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has described the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC’s decision to postpone the clean-up of the national voters’ register until after the 2027 general elections as a major failure. The party said INEC had four years to prepare for the exercise. However, ADC said the voters’ register is only one of several issues that will determine the credibility of the 2027 elections. They pointed to electronic transmission of results, result collation and compliance with the Electoral Act as other major areas of concern. Speaking to Vanguard, the ADC National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, said INEC’s failure to clean up the register raised questions about its commitment to conducting credible elections. “This shouldn’t have happened. INEC had four years to prepare and plan for this, and its failure to do so does not suggest that it is taking its responsibilities seriously, particularly the issue of maintaining a credible voters’ register,” he said. Abdullahi, however, said the party would not make the outcome of the 2027 elections depend solely on whether INEC produced a credible voters’ register, noting that previous elections had been conducted despite imperfections in the register. “We do not believe that the credibility of the 2027 general election rests solely on INEC’s ability to produce a credible voters’ register. It would have given everyone greater confidence if the commission had been able to do so, but we are not going to hinge the fate of the 2027 election on that single issue.” He said the ADC was also concerned about how INEC would implement the Electoral Act, particularly the electronic transmission of results from polling units, the collation process and the duties of electoral officers regarding Forms EC8A and EC8E. “There are other, more pertinent issues of concern to our party. These include compliance with the Electoral Act, the electronic transmission of results from polling units, the collation of results and the additional responsibilities assigned to electoral officers regarding Forms EC8A and EC8E.” On the possible effect of the voters’ register on the elections, Abdullahi argued that strict compliance with the law, particularly provisions on voter accreditation, could reduce the impact of its shortcomings. “If INEC complies with the Electoral Act, particularly regarding voter accreditation, the shortcomings in the voters’ register may not have as much impact. Problems arise when the commission fails to abide by its own rules and the provisions of the Electoral Act,” he said. He said the ADC was studying possible weaknesses in the electoral process and making arrangements to ensure that its votes were protected. “We know where the loopholes are, and that is why we continue to focus on them and ensure that we make adequate arrangements to protect our votes.” Vanguard News The post 2027 Election: INEC failed on voters’ register – ADC appeared first

nigeria.description: Global players’ union FIFPRO has slammed Bayern Munich for putting pressure on midfielder Jamal Musiala to renegotiate his contract with the Bundesliga club as he recovers from injury. In a statement issued Saturday, the footballers’ union said recent public comments made by Bayern’s honorary president Uli Hoeness, current CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen and former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge were part of a “coordinated campaign” to put pressure on Musiala. The Bayern bosses had questioned whether Musiala, who missed several matches with a neurological condition earlier in the season and has recently returned from a hamstring injury, should continue to receive his contracted salary. FIFPRO hit out at “a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations”. “A club of Bayern’s standing should know better,” the international union for professional football players said. “Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala… Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives. “Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.” The 23-year-old Germany international signed a contract extension in February 2025 until 2030 and is among Bayern’s top earners. nigeria.title: China Diaries: The Railway Connecting Continents
nigeria.description: Standing at the Xi’an International Port Station in northwest China, watching the movement of freight trains preparing to transport goods across borders and continents, I was reminded that economic development is not only about what a country produces. It is also about how efficiently it can move what it produces to the rest of the world. Xi’an occupies an interesting place in China’s history. It was once the starting point of the ancient Silk Road, which connected China to Central Asia, the Middle East and Europe through centuries of trade and cultural exchange. Today, the city is reclaiming that historic role through a modern railway network that connects Chinese manufacturing centres to markets across Europe and Asia. The China-Europe Railway Express is one of the most visible outcomes of China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). Through this network, freight trains transport automobiles, electronics, machinery, textiles, agricultural products and other goods across the Eurasian continent. What makes the initiative particularly interesting is how it has transformed the economic possibilities of a city located thousands of kilometres from the sea. Xi’an has become an important international logistics hub, demonstrating that geographical distance from a coastline does not have to limit a city’s participation in global trade. The railway network has continued to expand. By November 2025, China-Europe freight trains had completed nearly 120,000 journeys, connecting 232 cities in 26 European countries and more than 100 cities in 11 Asian countries. The value of goods transported through the network had reached $426.4 billion by the end of 2024. These are not merely impressive transportation figures. They represent an evolving system of economic connectivity, linking manufacturers, suppliers, distributors and consumers across national borders. Beyond transportation: The economics of connectivity The significance of the railway goes beyond moving containers from one destination to another. It creates opportunities for businesses to reach markets faster, diversify their supply chains and reduce their dependence on a single transportation route. Rail freight offers an important middle ground between air and sea transportation. While it is generally more expensive than shipping by sea, it can be considerably faster. For certain categories of goods, particularly machinery, automobile components, electronics and other time-sensitive products, that difference can be commercially significant. nigeria.title: English village votes to ‘leave UK’ over migrant camp plan
nigeria.description: A small English village on Saturday voted to leave the UK in a symbolic poll protesting government plans to house hundreds of asylum seekers at a nearby former air force base. The vote in Barnham follows a similar protest referendum in the village of Piddington in September, also over government plans to move asylum seekers from hotels into former military accommodation. Between 400 to 500 people were eligible to vote in the ballot which carried no legal weight, with 257 voting for independence, 16 against, and one spoilt ballot. “There’s an issue with the sheer volume of people expected to be accommodated,” the chairwoman of the Barnham residents’ association, Helen Beck, told AFP earlier. “Barnham is a small village. There will be nothing for the (lodged) people to do, nowhere to go.” Under plans by Britain’s government, the base near the village in rural eastern England will be used to accommodate 931 migrants. The village has a population of 584. Residents were asked whether they supported seeking a “crown dependency status” similar to that of Jersey, Guernsey and the Isle of Man. Parish council chair John Bauer said this would allow the village to “retain loyalty to the crown” while removing itself from Home Office jurisdiction. – Safety concern – Residents in both Barnham and Piddington say they are also worried about locals’ safety, particularly that of women. “We’ve been told they (the asylum seekers) are all males. We don’t know where they are from, their background,” Beck said. “People are anxious about walking alone, walking their dog in darkness if an additional 900 men arrive in the area,” she said. In the Piddington vote in September, 285 out of 312 votes were cast in favour of “pursuing self-determination”. The government plans to house around 1,250 asylum seekers on a former defence ministry site close to Piddington village, all single men between 18 and 65. Britain’s centre-left government, in power since July 2024, has vowed to end the use of hotels as migrant accommodation following a public outcry. It plans to move all those currently in hotels — a policy inherited from the last Conservative government — to former military bases by 2029. But Beck said that there were questions about whether military-style accommodation was suitable for people “fleeing a conflict or persecution”, adding that it was also “significantly more expensive than hotels”. entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. entertainment.title: Esther Adeyanju: This International Men’s Day, Let’s Make Room for Men’s Vulnerability
entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. entertainment.description: Tems receiving the Best African Music Performance at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards. In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. Its creation was a recognition of how far African music had travelled globally, and Nigerian artists were at the centre of that movement. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. While South African artist Tyla has won the award twice, more than any individual Nigerian artist, Nigerian artists have consistently enjoyed greater representation in the nominations. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. However, I believe it is the responsibility of an award of this repute to look beyond the most visible names and recognise the best African music released within its eligibility period. A song should not earn a nomination simply because it is popular or has enjoyed international success. sports.title: Chelsea’s deep and ongoing issues revealed by Leeds drubbing
sports.description: By the end, amid what Xabi Alonso described as a “fragile moment”, even his own cultured touch had deserted him. As his Chelsea team tried to offer something in the final minutes of an utterly nothing performance against a brilliant Leeds United , the ball was easily cleared for a throw. Alonso, famed for his technique as a player, miscontrolled it towards his underwhelming bench. He’s now seeing his reputation as a coach plummet, as Chelsea fall to eighth. This 4-1 evisceration was not just Leeds’ first win at the home of their old Seventies rivals since 1999 – to add to how Tottenham Hotspur also won here a few weeks ago – but a second defeat in a row, and a fifth in 11 this season. And yet the very nature of it was still worse than any numbers can tell. Outside an early Emmanuel Emegha goal on his first start, there was nothing to speak positively about, and just nothing about Chelsea. Leeds found it easy to get at them, and they were soon rampaging through them. They could have been 3-1 up by half-time, after Noah Okafor’s well-taken equaliser, but it never looked like it would take long to get there in the second half. And, sure, Chelsea might well dispute the absurd-looking handball decision that eventually gave Dominic Calvert-Lewin his goal to make it 2-1, but they couldn’t dispute that it was coming. Leeds were rampant, Okafor soon lashing in his second from yet another poorly-defended set-piece. There, Austin MacPhee’s influence becomes just one more aspect to question about the first team. The manner of Brenden Aaronson’s goal, as he was allowed to just surge through the team, summed the afternoon up. Chelsea didn’t look a team. Leeds, by contrast, knew exactly what they were about in every moment of the game. They had an identity. Chelsea are instead looking to individuals. Emmanuel Emegha scored Chelsea’s goal (Reuters) They lost all cohesion once Moises Caicedo again went off injured, having already lacked any bite without Joao Pedro . The striker was nevertheless involved in what might actually have been one of the match’s most telling moments. As Cole Palmer went off, Chelsea coach Willie Isa seemed to gesture the forward towards the fans. There were admittedly very few left, and many of those had loudly booed on the final whistle. Palmer didn’t go over, and then seemed to have a few words with Joao Pedro, too. They didn’t look all that amicable. “We were disappointed,” Alonso said afterwards. Either way, there is probably a bigger point there, that emphasises how all this is bigger than the manager. Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s penalty sent Leeds ahead (Reuters) Yes, a coach as accomplished as Alonso should be doing better than this. sports.description: Malick Thiaw put Newcastle in front against Arsenal (ANDY BUCHANAN) Arsenal missed the chance to open up an eight-point lead at the top of the Premier League after a stirring second-half fightback from Newcastle held the defending champions to a 2-2 draw on Saturday. The Gunners led through Eberechi Eze's strike after a dominant first 45 minutes. But Mikel Arteta's men were suddenly headed for defeat when goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw provided a much-needed boost for under-fire Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle. Noni Madueke salvaged a point for Arsenal and stretched their lead at the top over surprise package Brighton to six points. However, the loss of influential goalkeeper David Raya to injury could provide a twist in the title race that many believed Arsenal would cruise. Newcastle remain in the bottom half of the table with just one win in six games in all competitions. Yet, Jaissle can point to his side's second half performance as a potential turning point after a difficult start to his reign at St. James' Park. Arsenal move back six points clear of third-placed Manchester City, but missed the chance to put their foot down in the defence of their title. Madueke continued his impressive form in the injury absence of Bukayo Saka and hit the post early on. Former Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes was roundly booed on his first return to Tyneside since making a £75 million ($98 million) move to the Emirates Stadium In August. The Brazilian nearly silenced his former faithful when he prodded just wide from a Madueke cross as Arsenal pressed for the opener. It duly arrived 10 minutes before the break when Kai Havertz pounced on a poor touch by Lewis Hall and brilliantly played in Eze to blast high past Lukas Hornicek. Jaissle got the response he needed from his half-time team talk as Newcastle came out a completely different proposition after the break. Arsenal also played a part in letting the home side back into the game and lifting the 50,000 crowd in doing so. Martin Odegaard shanked his attempt at a long ball forward to allow William Osula to play in Barnes to level. Suddenly an Arsenal side that had kept seven clean sheets in their opening 10 league games was on the rocks. Thiaw bundled home a second for Newcastle just 13 minutes later after Dan Burn was left completely unmarked from a corner and his header was only parried by Raya. That proved to be one of Raya's final interventions as the Spaniard had to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga. Raya would be a massive miss if the Spaniard is sidelined for a significant spell. But Arsenal regained their composure in time to salvage a point that keeps them well in the driving seat to retain the title. Odegaard made amends for his earlier error by freeing Madueke down the right and he cut inside before his tame deflected shot found a way past Hornicek. kca/nf

sports.title: Cardinals make bad Carson Beck news official for Week 11 vs. Chiefs
sports.description: Cardinals make bad Carson Beck news official for Week 11 vs. Chiefs originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Arizona Cardinals have shuffled through multiple quarterbacks this season, starting with Jacoby Brissett for a few weeks. Gardner Minshew then got a chance, but he recently got hurt. Carson Beck stepped in, making his NFL debut and first start in Week 10. While he and the Cardinals struggled in a loss to the Los Angeles Rams , it was still nice to see Beck make his first appearance in the NFL. But the following practice week didn't go well, as back spasms sidelined him. Unfortunately, as Cardinals reporter Darren Urban shared , the team made it official: Beck is out and won't face the Kansas City Chiefs . Cardinals officially rule out Carson Beck "The AZCardinals officially downgrade QB Carson Beck to OUT for Sunday's game because of back spasms," Urban reports. "Josh Johnson gets the start in K.C." While this Cardinals team isn't contending for anything this season, one of the more important things to take away from this year is how their young players perform. It might have a low chance of happening, but if Beck impresses this season, they might have an interesting question to ask themselves at the quarterback position this upcoming offseason. But with Beck now set to miss Week 11 due to back spasms, that evaluation is on hold. Josh Johnson, the ultimate journeyman quarterback, will get the start for Arizona against the Chiefs this weekend. Beck isn't the only one this Cardinals' offense will be missing. Brissett and Marvin Harrison Jr. were traded; Minshew, James Connor, Jeremiyah Love, Kendrick Bourne, Michael Wilson, and Jalen Brooks are all out due to injury. MORE : Blake Corum extends impressive touchdown streak as Rams continue remarkable turnaround Tyler Allgeier, Zonovan Knight, Trey McBride, Elijah Higgins, Simi Fehoko, Reggie Virgil, Devin Duvernay, and Harrison Wallace III make up the skill players for the Cardinals in Week 11. So, while seeing Beck play is important, it would not be a surprise if he struggled with such a lackluster supporting cast, especially going up against a tough Chiefs defense, like the tough unit he faced in his NFL debut. After Beck completed 11 of 18 passes for 108 yards and no touchdowns with two picks against the Rams in Week 10, he's now going to miss his next chance to start with a back problem. The Cardinals have officially ruled out Beck for Week 11, turning to Johnson as their fourth staring quarterback they've turned to this season. sports.title: Lake Creek sweeps Abilene Wylie to win first volleyball state championship
sports.description: Lake Creek's won the school's first state volleyball championship Saturday. (Courtesy of Lake Creek Volleyball) Lake Creek volleyball coach Kayli Kane knew this year's team had a chance to be good. Really good. With plenty of returning talent and strong leadership from their senior group, the Lions made winning a state championship their goal from the beginning of the season. On Saturday in Garland, they made it a reality. Lake Creek earned a 25-19, 28-26, 25-14 sweep over Abilene Wylie to claim the UIL Class 5A Division II state title at the Curtis Culwell Center, marking the first championship in program history and the first for Montgomery ISD. The Lions (44-10) finished their season on an 11-match winning streak and ended a 23-match winning streak for Wylie (39-5), which was hoping to capture its first state championship since claiming the Class 3A title in 2012. Blaire Sexton led the Lions with 15 kills, 10 digs and four aces, while Ryan Mokry added 12 kills, 14 digs and six blocks. Alexis Hammack contributed nine kills and six blocks, and Breck Tessier finished with 36 assists. The tightest test came in the second set, when Lake Creek scored the final three points to turn a 26-25 deficit into a two-set lead. Hammack's kill gave the Lions a 27-26 advantage before a Wylie attack error ended the set. Lake Creek closed out the match with its most decisive set, punctuating the sweep with a kill from Mokry. The Lions finished with 10 aces and nine blocks while holding Wylie to a .040 hitting percentage. This is a developing story and will be updated. Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. sports.title: Rob Pelinka on Lakers: 'We’ll be active at the trade deadline'
sports.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 18: Austin Reaves #15, Luka Doncic #77, Jaden Hardy #7, Jarred Vanderbilt #2 and Jake LaRavia #12 of the Los Angeles Lakers on the bench during a 109-97 Utah Jazz win at Crypto.com Arena on November 18, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) Getty Images The Los Angeles Lakers sit on top of the Western Conference at 14-3, with the third-best offense in the NBA — behind an MVP-level start to the season from Luka Doncic — and a solid defense. Walker Kessler has been exactly what the Lakers hoped for as a big in the paint, and their moves for role players that better fit around Doncic — Matisse Thybulle, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Quentin Grimes, Quentin Grimes — have largely worked out. Lakers general manager Rob Pelinka has seen it, too, and thinks this team has a deep playoff run in them. Which is why he said in an interview on the Lakers pregame show that the team would be "active" at the trade deadline (hat tip Real GM ). "We'll be active at the trade deadline to shore up things that we see. We think this team has a real chance to make a run, so we want to give the group as much talent as we can. Don't want to get too far over our skis with a hot start, because you don't want to get big-headed, but clearly the way it's gone so far, it's been great, and we hope it continues." Active is a broad term. The Lakers will be active talking to teams, whether they make a deal will depend on the players available, and the price. The Lakers' most critical need is to improve at backup center behind Kessler. Kevon Looney has largely fallen out of the rotation, leaving the Lakers playing small ball with Sandro Mamukelashvili or Jarred Vanderbilt at the five, or leaning into two-way big Carson Cooper. There may be better options available. The Lakers don't have draft picks of note to trade, but they have players, and while they are hard-capped at the first apron, they are a little more than $8 million below that line and have room to work.

sports.title: Postseason Volleyball is Back: What to Know about the Nittany Lions
sports.description: LOUISVILLE, KENTUCKY - DECEMBER 22: The Penn St. Nittany Lions celebrate after defeating the Louisville Cardinals to win the Division I Women's Volleyball Championship held at the KFC YUM! Center on December 22, 2024 in Louisville, Kentucky. (Photo by Jamie Schwaberow/NCAA Photos via Getty Images) | NCAA Photos via Getty Images Note from Patrick: My former Onward State colleague, Steve Connelly, was kind enough to put together a postseason primer for the women’s volleyball team as they embark on their quest for another national title tomorrow. Get the lowdown on the Nittany Lions below! 2024 marked Penn State’s first NCAA volleyball title in a decade. 2025 saw the Nittany Lions suffer their worst season since joining the Big Ten. 2026? It’s been a mixed bag. Penn State didn’t have an RPI Top-25 win through 17 matches, racking up five losses in that stretch. Since, the team’s won 10 straight with four RPI top-25 wins and seven wins in the top 50. In mid-October, Penn State would’ve been lucky to get a top-16 seed that grants a team the right to host the first two rounds of the NCAA Tournament. Now, Big Ten Player of the Year Kennedy Martin and the Nittany Lions are in the running for one of the top four seeds, which would allow Penn State to host until the Final Four. Winning the inaugural Big Ten Volleyball Tournament might be enough to bring the Sweet 16 and Elite Eight back to Rec Hall. So what’s changed? Penn State has cleaned up its first contact when receiving serve, allowing its setter to choose between multiple attacking options and putting its pin hitters in better positions to score. The team’s passer rating – a 0-to-3 scale that grades serve receive based on how many attacking options that a pass gives a setter (a 3 meaning that a setter has the ability to set three players, a 2 meaning the setter can set two players, etc.) – often hovered around-or-below a 2 early in the season, which is not competitive against top teams. In Penn State’s five losses, the Nittany Lions were outpassed 2.24-to-2.03. From six matches against ranked opponents during their 10-game winning streak, the Nittany Lions passed at least a 2.1 in five of those matches. It’s not elite, but it is making a difference. The uptick in passer rating started when Penn State switched to a two-libero system. It’s a newer rule in NCAA volleyball allowing teams to designate two defensive-minded players per set in the different-colored jersey, with only one allowed on court at a time. Penn State uses this rule to play one libero, junior Ava Falduto, when the Nittany Lions are receiving serve, and the other libero, senior Jocelyn Nathan, when the Nittany Lions are serving. Essentially, it allows Falduto to focus on passing, while Nathan’s focus is on floor defense and digging the ball. sports.title: Inside Week 11 of CIAC football: Thanksgiving names, tournament bids and a regular season wrap
sports.description: North Branford's #5 Jack Sigel runs to the outside as Valley Regional/Lyme-Old Lyme's #12 Noah Rocha and #51 Paul Kuhn try to tackle during a CIAC high school football game at North Branford High School, Thursday, November 19, 2026. (Dave Zajac/Hearst Connecticut Media) We've reached the end of the line for the 2026 CIAC football regular season. Now the fun really begins. Thanksgiving football is on deck and, for 48 teams, the playoffs beyond. With at least a third of the tournament spots still open according to GametimeCT's unofficial calculations , there's plenty of drama in the final week. After a somewhat lackluster first half of the season, the second half paid off with plenty of electric games, led by Ludlowe's 34-31 win over New Canaan on Oct. 30, a game which had a wild momentum swing and jumbled the GametimeCT Top 10 Poll . The season has featured some great quarterback play, highlighted by seven senior veterans , at least six of whom will soon be in the playoff spotlight. And the list goes deeper than just those seven. For the holiday week ahead, there are 56 games involving 111 CIAC teams, with Stonington's long-running series with Westerly (R.I.) accounting for that odd number. Thanksgiving week holds plenty of drama outside of the playoff picture, with trophies, rivalry wins and bragging rights part of the scene. And the names are definitely cool. There's the Beehive Bowl between East Haven and Branford (Yellowjackets and Hornets, get it?), the Apple Valley Classic between Southington and Cheshire ; the Air and Speed Bowl between the Stafford and Windsor co-ops ; the 75th Green Bowl between Notre Dame-West Haven and Hamden ; and the Olde Canal Cup between Farmington and Plainville . Map fans will have a blast. There's the 7-Mile Bowl between Platt Tech and O'Brien Tech ; the Route 17 Bowl between the Coginchaug co-op and North Branford ; the Battle of Route 83 between Rockville and Ellington ; and even the Clash Along County Lines between the Valley Panthers and Griswold/Wheeler . Battles are also plentiful. There's a battle for a Boot ( Oxford-Derby ), Helmet ( Torrington-Watertown ), Bell ( Bristol Central-Bristol Eastern ), and Sword ( Ledyard-Fitch ), as well as a Battle of the Bay ( Waterford-East Lyme ). Intense rivalries are also in play, including the Stoddard Bowl between Maloney and Platt , both of whom call Falcon Field in Meriden home; the annual showdown between Ansonia and Naugatuck ; and the Turkey Bowl between New Canaan and Darien . Some of the longest-running series include Wilbur Cross , now co-oping with Career , against Hillhouse ; and the aforementioned Westerly (R.I) against Stonington . But for longevity, nothing holds a candle to New London vs. Norwich Free Academy , a series which started way back in 1875 and is the country's oldest rivalry. Enjoy the football and turkey. sports.title: Five Known Suitors For Freddy Peralta Revealed By Insider; Rays, Padres, Cubs Involved
sports.description: Free agent pitcher Freddy Peralta Freddy Peralta is one of the best free agents available this winter, and there is reportedly a ton of interest in him. According to The Athletic's Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon , "half a dozen or so teams" are involved in Peralta's market, but not all of the suitors are known. The Athletic named the Tampa Bay Rays, Chicago Cubs, Chicago White Sox, Toronto Blue Jays and San Diego Padres as the known suitors for the two-time All-Star. He would be a great addition to any of those teams, but he seems due for a nine-figure payday, and not every team can afford that. The Padres and Cubs have the biggest need for starting pitching among the teams listed. The Blue Jays and Padres are also reportedly involved in signing Tarik Skubal. If the Blue Jays or Padres are willing to spend on Skubal, they will surely have the money to pay Peralta if they need to pivot. Peralta started off the season poorly with the New York Mets. However, the Rays acquired him at the trade deadline and made some changes to get him back to pitching like an All-Star. He had a 0.79 ERA in his final six regular-season starts and was great in the postseason as well. His lone blemish in the final two months of play was his dud in the World Series against a relentless Milwaukee Brewers offense. Peralta was the American League Championship Series MVP, and he can be an ace on many staffs around the league. More MLB: How Does Royce Lewis Fit On Dodgers After Reported Trade?

(Arnold Gold/Hearst Connecticut Media) WETHERSFIELD - Three years, two semifinal heartbreaks and a job finally finished. The Ludlowe field hockey team won its first CIAC championship Saturday in Wethersfield, beating No. 1 seed and defending champion Darien 2-1 to cap a mission that started when the current players were playing at the youth level. Darien had beaten Ludlowe twice previously this season, once in the regular season and again two weeks ago in the FCIAC championship game. "Looking back at that last game, I don't think we put up enough of a fight and made it easy for them to put in goals early against us," Ludlowe junior Lily McClay said. "This is a dream come true and means everything. I thought about this game every day and said a prayer every night and it finally happened." Ludlowe took an early lead with 3:24 left in the first quarter when Lily's sister, freshman Emerson McClay, kept the ball alive on the end line and was able to sneak it past the goalie for the crucial first goal. "When I insert (on corners), I try to go for rebounds and it was there and, to be honest, I didn't know if I was in the circle or not, and I was so happy when it went in," Emerson McClay said. "I wasn't sure if it was going to count, but it got us going." Emerson McClay would add a second goal with 5:45 left in the second quarter, putting Ludlowe up 2-0 at halftime. Darien would not go away and cut the deficit to one on a Skylar Stephens goal with 6:30 left. From there, the clock could not move fast enough for Ludlowe. "That was forever, the longest five minutes of my life, but we handled it well," Ludlowe coach Laura McClay, Lily and Emerson's mother, said. "We are thrilled. I could not be happier for this group and these seniors." Darien was playing in its fifth straight Class L final and 19th overall, but did not have enough to snag back-to-back titles. "From the get-go, the ball wasn't bouncing our way," Darien coach Mo Minicus said. "They went up 2-0 with our mistakes, but we hung in there and fought and out-cornered them and out-shot them, but their goalie played great. We didn't get the tips, we didn't get the rebounds, but I am proud of the girls and proud of their fight." Ludlowe goalie Erin McNamara made eight saves, including one diving effort in the first half to preserve the lead. Player of the Game Lily McClay, Ludlowe: Her sister got the two goals, but McClay's dominant stickhandling all afternoon helped lead Ludlowe. Quotable "It has been about sticking to the process, putting the work in and having a great two weeks since we saw Darien last. We tried to correct things and keep our composure. The defense has been working their butts off and that really helped us today." - Ludlowe coach Laura McClay. technology.title: AWS got hit by an outage too. Here's why you didn't hear about it
technology.description: My editor asked me this week "why is everything except AWS breaking?" It's a great question! They haven't been in the headlines! In fact, as they are wont to do, AWS spokesperson Patrick Neighorn g ot salty to a reporter about how unreliable Downdetector is when it started showing them as impacted. If you'll permit me a small digression, this stems from a misunderstanding of what Downdetector is for. Historically the AWS status site was so hilariously slow to reflect the lived customer experience that some jackass (me) built a rewriter that sits at stop.lying.cloud to make it a smidgen more realistic. As a result, the question people are really trying to answer when they visit Downdetector is "my app just broke; is it my crappy code or is there a global event going on?" There are mitigations for both, but they look nothing alike. AWS view crowdsourced reports of the form "the internet is broken, must be AWS" as a stain upon their honor. In fact, it's a badge of their own success, as "the internet" and "AWS" have become inextricably linked in people's minds. But back to my editor's question, "why didn't AWS go down?" Easy: it did. Everything breaks, all the time, including the narrative AWS now has 34 generally available commercial regions, of which two are currently smoking craters due to the Iran conflict. Each of these has hundreds of services that AWS offers to customers, of which a dozen or so are high quality, if I'm being characteristically uncharitable. They experience degradation in various ways, and they go largely unnoticed. But on November 15, AWS confirmed an incident that disrupted 11 of those ~12 good services in their oldest and most important region, us-east-1. At 3:05 AM PST, they stated that they started seeing sign-up errors, authentication issues, and connectivity issues. Five minutes later engineers were engaged. Not to be outdone, their status page swung into action after a leisurely coffee, and posted its first indication of an incident 93 minutes later. (See previous comments on stop.lying.cloud ). The all-clear showed up at 6:53 AM. Every site has downtime. Sometimes it blows up publicly, other times nobody seems to notice. Heck, AWS said in September that it had experienced permanent data loss in its two smoking craters, but after that news cycle passed I haven't heard a thing about it. I do think it's patently unreasonable to blame them for this specific problem; "acts of war" are kinda hard to predict from the corporate planning meeting. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

science.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. He even calls Worf — not a man renowned for dodging a fight — a coward, prompting the Klingon to respond that, "If you were any other man, I would kill you where you stand." Ouch. But following some impassioned talk about making the Borg "pay for what they've done", he's finally talked down from his rage by 21st-century stowaway Lily Sloane (Alfre Woodard). She points out that his Moby-Dick-esque obsession is on the verge of going full Ahab, and he eventually sees sense, issuing the order to abandon the Enterprise and destroy the hive. It's a masterclass showcasing the ever-brilliant Stewart's impressive range, as the out-of-control captain's rarely seen temper reaches fever pitch, before normal service is resumed. His subsequent apology to Worf — "As a matter of fact, I think you're the bravest man I've ever known" — is simply perfect. And just as the franchise's zenith, "The Wrath of Khan", is built around Kirk and Khan's decades-old feud, "First Contact" is precision engineered to get the most out of Jean-Luc. This was the right "Star Trek" at the right time, a film that put "TNG"'s greatest villains on a collision course with the origins of Starfleet. science.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
science.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Before Flight 15, SpaceX had already caught Starship's first-stage booster, known as Super Heavy, on three separate occasions , and it had reflown a booster twice. But the company had never attempted a Ship catch, which is a taller order, given how much faster and farther Starship upper stages fly. So snagging Ship on the first try was a very big deal, according to Musk. "Everyone knew, within SpaceX, at least, how important this milestone was, and that it was really something fundamental and profound — that Starship will be the first-ever fully reusable orbital space system," he told Baker and Gracias on Wednesday. The Ship upper stage of SpaceX's Starship megarocket comes back to its launch tower for a "chopsticks" catch on Nov. 14, 2026, during the vehicle's 15th test flight. (Image credit: SpaceX) And SpaceX is very serious about Starship reuse. Musk has said that the company wants to launch about 10,000 Starship missions per year by 2030. This mind-boggling cadence will help the company build out two enormous megaconstellations in low Earth orbit — the next iteration of its Starlink broadband network, which will consist of about 100,000 satellites , and its Starmind AI data-center constellation, which will be 10 times bigger than that . science.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
science.description: null Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the solar system's innermost planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Today's orbital insertion is the latest milestone in BepiColombo's Mercury arrival phase, which is expected to take about six months in total. Arrival began on Sept. 3, when the MTM released MPO and Mio. The two orbiters remain connected today; they won't separate until Dec. 9 or thereabouts. Shortly thereafter, Mio will settle into its final orbit, a highly elliptical path that will take it over Mercury's poles. MPO is also destined for a polar orbit, though a much less elliptical one than Mio's; the ESA probe will conduct a series of engine burns before finally getting there on March 10, 2027. BepiColombo won't start doing science work until April 6, 2027. The two probes will gather complementary data from their two different vantage points, shedding a great deal of light on a mysterious world. "The mission will study all aspects of Mercury, from the structure and dynamics of its magnetosphere and how it interacts with the solar wind , to its internal structure with its large iron core, and the origin of the planet’s magnetic field," ESA officials wrote in a BepiColombo mission description . "The data will enable scientists to understand more about the origin and evolution of a planet located close to its parent star, and a better understanding of the overall evolution of our solar system," they added.

A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317. The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on Nov. 20, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX ended its launch webcast just after that touchdown, so we didn't get to see the Falcon 9's upper stage power its way to orbit. USSF-317 is a classified mission, so we don't know what the upper stage is carrying or where exactly it's headed. However, some experts think that USSF-317 may be hauling a batch of SpaceX's Starshield satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO) for the Space Force's Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio, which helps the military keep tabs on potential targets around the world. science.title: What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental?
science.description: Bernhard Riemann set out a problem mathematicians have been trying solve for more than a century The Granger Collection/Alamy The cadence of prime numbers has a pattern; it isn’t simply chaos. Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. The proof of the Reimann hypothesis is also one of the Clay Mathematics Institute ’s Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million prize for a solution. Advertisement The Riemann hypothesis has loomed so large over mathematicians for decades because it concerns mathematics’ most simple yet hard-to-understand objects: prime numbers . These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. He hypothesised that the way primes are spaced throughout the number line can be inferred from another set of numbers, now tied to a mathematical function called the Riemann zeta function. These numbers are complex – so each is actually a pair of numbers, one called real and one called imaginary – and when they are plugged into the Riemann zeta function, the function spits out zero. Confusingly, these numbers that result in a zero from the function are called “non-trivial zeros”. Riemann discovered that summing over a sequence of these complex numbers allowed him to predict the distribution of primes up to a certain high number. Effectively, he came upon a formula that could make sense of primes’ seemingly random appearances among numbers. science.title: Don't turn the moon into the Wild West, scientists warn
science.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment. Two such researchers are Florian Rabitz, a professor of climate and technology governance at Vilnius University in Lithuania, and Xiao-Shan Yap, an assistant professor of Earth-space sustainability at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a piece published last month in the journal Global Environmental Politics , the pair call for "robust international regulations" and "broad and inclusive deliberation" to allow the global community to carefully consider the impact of economic activities on the moon. In addition to the threat to the scientifically priceless lunar landscape, the researchers also object to the colonization of the moon by a small number of powerful players — namely China, the U.S. and their respective close allies. "With the moon it's absolutely clear that whoever is doing the big infrastructure work is going to be asserting their position, including by defining their own exclusive territories," Rabitz said in a statement . "That shouldn't be the Wild West." Rabitz pointed out that, although the United Nations' 1967 Outer Space Treaty prevents individual nations from appropriating the moon, Earth's natural satellite and its valuable resources are unlikely to remain truly neutral territory if its exploitation is going to be led by a small number of powerful nations.
